title: All of HUMANITY Fits in a Sugar Cube ☕
description:
Guess how many people fit in your sugar cube. All of them! Every atom in you is like cotton candy: a big fluffy cloud of almost nothing around one tiny speck that carries nearly all the weight. Squash the fluff out of all 8 billion of us and the whole of humanity would fit in ONE sugar cube. Squashed on your own? A speck too small to see... that still weighs as much as you.
What was your guess?

The science: the centre of an atom (its nucleus) is about 100,000 times smaller across than the atom, yet it holds more than 99.9% of the mass. Matter with the empty space squeezed out (nuclear density) is about 230 million tonnes per cubic centimetre. All of humanity weighs very roughly 400-500 million tonnes, so it would fill about 2 cubic centimetres: one sugar cube. One 62 kg person would be a speck about 6 micrometres across, smaller than the eye can see. It's a thought experiment: ordinary atoms can't be squashed like this. Only a neutron star does it for real.
